title: When can you fall back from eID to remote document checks under the EU AML Regulation (AMLR), and how do you record it? | Customer Due Diligence Guide
summary: Under AMLA's draft CDD RTS, remote document checks may replace eID only in limited cases. When the fallback is allowed and what to record.
body_markdown:
*When AMLA's draft standards allow remote document checks instead of eID, which safeguards the process needs and what to record to justify each case to the supervisor.*


Under AMLA's draft regulatory technical standards on customer due diligence (CDD RTS), a business may verify a customer remotely with a document instead of an eID only when the customer cannot reasonably be expected to present an identity document in person and has access to neither qualifying electronic identification means nor relevant qualified trust services. The business must be able to justify each such case, and it keeps customer due diligence records for 5 years after the end of the business relationship, after the occasional transaction is carried out, or after it refuses to establish the relationship or carry out the transaction.


*Written by Aleksander Wasiak (Compliance Officer) and Helena Suska (Head of Customer Success), Authologic.*
